title: SIM Only Deals Explained: Save Without a New Phone
description: How SIM only plans work in the UK: 30-day vs 12-month deals, how much data you need, which network each brand uses and how to switch and keep your number.
h1: SIM only: keep your phone, cut your bill
intro: If your phone still works well, a SIM-only plan is usually the cheapest way to stay connected. You just pay for calls, texts and data, with no phone cost baked in.

blocks.title: Going SIM only in four steps

items.title: Check your contract
items.text: Has your phone been paid off? If your contract has ended, you may be paying for a phone you already own.

items.title: Check your phone is unlocked
items.text: Phones sold in the UK since December 2021 are sold unlocked. Older phones may need unlocking by your network.

items.title: Pick a network, then a plan
items.text: Choose coverage first, then the brand and data amount that suit you.

items.title: Keep your number
items.text: Text PAC to 65075 and give the code to your new provider. The switch happens within one working day.

sections.html: 30-day plans let you leave or change with a month’s notice: great for flexibility and for trying a network. 12-month plans can be cheaper per month but tie you in, and some include price rises during the term. Always read the contract summary.

sections.h2: How much data do you need?
sections.html:
• Light: messaging, maps and email, mostly on wi-fi. A small allowance is often enough.
  • Medium: social media, music streaming and some video away from wi-fi.
  • Heavy: video streaming, hotspotting a laptop or working on the go. Consider a large or unlimited plan.

Check your phone’s settings for your average monthly use over the last few months. That’s your best guide.

• EU roaming: many plans now charge daily fees abroad. See our roaming guide.
  • 5G and speed caps: some cheap plans cap speeds or exclude 5G.
  • Wi-fi calling and eSIM: useful if indoor signal is weak, or for dual-SIM phones.
  • Data rollover: some brands let unused data carry over.

faqs.q: Will a SIM-only deal work in my phone?
faqs.a: Yes, if your phone is unlocked and supports the network’s bands (almost all modern phones do). Check whether you need a physical SIM or can use an eSIM.

faqs.q: Can I keep my number on a SIM-only plan?
faqs.a: Yes. Text PAC to 65075 from your current phone, then give the code to your new provider when you order.
